outcome: A land card in hand can be played only in a main phase of its owner's turn with an empty stack and priority, and it goes straight to the battlefield without using the stack.
A player can play one land per turn unless an effect raises the number.
A land play is legal exactly when lands allowed this turn exceed lands already played this turn, counting all ways of playing lands.
A land play is illegal once the allowed number is no greater than the number already played, even if an effect instructs it.
A land cannot be played on another player's turn, even if an effect instructs it.
A land put onto the battlefield by an effect does not count toward the lands played this turn.
A land with a basic land type has the mana ability for that type's color, regardless of its text.
Setting a land's subtype to basic land types removes its old land types and rules-text abilities and grants the matching mana abilities; adding types keeps the old ones.
A card that is a land and another type cannot be cast as a spell, only played as a land.
